scenarios.title: Selfdestruct-and-Redeploy Identity Confusion
scenarios.briefing: Unmapped attack surface identified by the Surface Engine (coverage 33%). Uncovered — never debated, no scenario. Exploitation mechanism: Force destruction and redeployment so the new implementation inherits legacy allowances. Invariant at risk: A contract that selfdestructs and is redeployed at the same address lets the new code inherit approvals and trust granted to the old one. Target architecture: Destructible Contract with Address-Reuse Dependency. Reference class: CWE-668 · Severity: High. The council has no prior debate on this surface. Treat it as uncharted: establish the mechanism, state the invariant, and identify where the defense actually fails.
scenarios.coreHypothesis: A contract that selfdestructs and is redeployed at the same address lets the new code inherit approvals and trust granted to the old one.

scenarios.title: ERC-4337 Validation Rule Bypass
scenarios.briefing: Unmapped attack surface identified by the Surface Engine (coverage 0%). Uncovered — never debated, no external intel, no scenario. Exploitation mechanism: Craft a UserOperation whose validationData satisfies the validator without the intended signer. Invariant at risk: A UserOperation validator that mis-scopes a signature check permits an operation to be sponsored by an account whose owner never authorized it. scenarios.title: Aggregate Signature Forgery on Attestation Sets
scenarios.briefing: Unmapped attack surface identified by the Surface Engine (coverage 0%). Uncovered — never debated, no external intel, no scenario. Exploitation mechanism: Forge an aggregate signature over a subset of votes and reuse it as evidence of wider participation. Invariant at risk: If BLS aggregate verification does not bind the participant bitmap to the signed message, an attacker can present a valid aggregate that hides which signers actually participated. Target architecture: BLS Aggregate Attestation Layer. Reference class: CWE-347 · Severity: Critical. The council has no prior debate on this surface. Treat it as uncharted: establish the mechanism, state the invariant, and identify where the defense actually fails.
scenarios.coreHypothesis: If BLS aggregate verification does not bind the participant bitmap to the signed message, an attacker can present a valid aggregate that hides which signers actually participated.
